results.text: 27 Global Poverty: Stalled Pro GreSS and riSinG Con Centration Welfare growth in MENAAP has shown a concerning pattern. Between 2000 and 2019, welfare grew modestly, at around 1.5 percent annually, across most of the distribution. However, welfare growth among the poorest percentiles has turned negative since 2020, even as incomes higher in the distribution have continued to grow modestly. This means that the poorest are not only failing to escape poverty, but are falling farther behind. Both insufficient growth and high levels of inequality limit how effectively growth translates into poverty reduction. Since 2010, per capita incomes in low-income economies have barely risen, averaging less than 0.1 percent growth annually (World Bank 2025a). context_chunks.text: 27 Global Poverty: Stalled Pro GreSS and riSinG Con Centration Welfare growth in MENAAP has shown a concerning pattern. Between 2000 and 2019, welfare grew modestly, at around 1.5 percent annually, across most of the distribution. However, welfare growth among the poorest percentiles has turned negative since 2020, even as incomes higher in the distribution have continued to grow modestly. This means that the poorest are not only failing to escape poverty, but are falling farther behind. Both insufficient growth and high levels of inequality limit how effectively growth translates into poverty reduction. Since 2010, per capita incomes in low-income economies have barely risen, averaging less than 0.1 percent growth annually (World Bank 2025a).
